lines: recin par diſette, & neceſſité, vn blaſpheme cõtre Dieu,
maledicence contre le Prince, iniure contre ſon pro-
chain, par vn gliſſement, & lubricité de langue: mais
vne calomnie eſt touſiours diliberee, conſpiree, & ma-
licieuſement pourpenſee: en deteſtation de laquelle, le
Seigneur Dieu ne ſ'eſt pas contenté de nons inſtruire
par la bouche de Moyſe, à ne baſtir aucune calomnie
contre noſtre prochain {f}: mais encor, eſtroictement
commandé deliurer l'oppreſſé de la main du calomnia
teur, à fin que ſon indignation n'entre comme le feu,
& enflambee pour la malice de telles affections, ne ſe
trouue apres qui la puiſſe eſtaindre {g}. Pareillement il a
donné pluſieurs grans, & propres epithetes à Satan
pour monſtrer ſa cruauté, & aſtuce malicieuſe. cõme
quand il l'a appellé, Serpent {h}, Dragon {i}, Aſpic {k}, Lion
rauiſſant, & bruiant {l}, mais entre tous n'a point voulu
oublier celuy qui luy eſt des plus conuenables, à
ſçauoir de le nommer Calomniateur, {m} partant qu'il eſt
vn menſonger, & faulx accuſateur qui ne tache inceſ-
ſamment qu'a mettre en confuſion noſtre conſcience,
pour nous faire trouuer mauuais, ce que par la grace
de Dieu nous auons bien fait. & au contraire, exauçant,
& magnifiant nos mauuaiſes œuures: que pour nous
entretenir, & endurcir en icelles. Il n'eſt certainement
crime en vne republique digne d'eſtre puni, & repri-
mé de ſi grande ſeuerité q'vne calomnie: & toutesfois
en ce malheureux ſiecle icy on ſ'en iouë, & les brides
ſe trouuent tellement laſchees aux calomniateurs, qu'il
leur eſt comme permis, auec impunité conſpirer, ordir,
& machiner toutes eſpeces de ruſes, cautelles & mechã-
cetez contre les gens de bien. O voix noble de Domi-
tian, qui diſoit, que le prince qui ne chaſtie point les ca-
lomniateurs, preſte la main a leur malice, & les ſouſtiẽt
{n}. Alexandre le Grand, quand il preſidoit au iugement
des crimes capitaux, auoit de couſtume pour obuier aux
calomnies, fermer de la main 'vne de ſes oreilles à fin
de la conſeruer entiere, & exẽpte de toute calomnie à
l'accuſé. & ſ'il pouuoit entendre, ou ſentir ſeulement l'o-
deur de quelque calomnie, il ſ'emflãboit de cou roux ſi
aigrement, qu'il ſe rendoit ſouuent cruel, & inexorable

uncertain.note: this note carries no printed key letter: at 4x and 8x the space to the left of the italic L is blank paper (nothing faint, no broken sort), so it is recorded with key null. By position and sense it is almost certainly the note for body marker {f} ('contre noſtre prochain {f}', the next line down, Leviticus xix being the commandment against false witness), but the key is not on the page.

uncertain.text: contre noſtre prochain {f}: mais encor, eſtroictement
uncertain.note: marker {f} has no margin note keyed f on this page; the unkeyed 'Leuit. c. xix.' note beside the line above is its likely citation (see margin_notes[1]). The marker itself is a clear italic f with a descender, and the point after it has two dots (colon), checked at 4x.

note key e has no {e} marker in the body of this page: the alphabet runs f–n here, so marker e must stand on p035 (not yet transcribed, so it could not be checked). The key letter of this note is a clear italic e.

uncertain.text: leur eſt comme permis, auec impunité conſpirer, ordir,
uncertain.note: a printed mark stands between 'eſt' and 'comme' and is NOT transcribed. Measured against neighbours on the same line: it is ~20px tall and 5-10px wide, its top at mid x-height, its foot resting on the baseline without crossing it. The period of 'fait.&' (line 21) is ~13x15px and sits wholly at the baseline; the colon of 'calomnie:' (line 25) spans ~34px with a clear gap between two square dots; the comma of 'permis,' on this same line descends ~10px below the baseline. The mark matches none of them: it is a narrow stroke with a blob at its foot, the same shape reader B noted between 'vertu' and its comma on p030. Read as a stray/broken sort rather than punctuation. If it is punctuation the likeliest candidates are a point or a comma.

uncertain.text: calomnies, fermer de la main 'vne de ſes oreilles à fin
uncertain.note: the mark between 'main' and 'vne' is a solid sort ~12px wide and ~20px tall standing wholly in the ascender zone (its foot at the x-height line), i.e. in apostrophe position; transcribed as an apostrophe. It may be the apostrophe of 'l'vne' whose l failed to print. A second, thinner mark between 'à' and 'fin' on the same line is a paper fibre/crease (it runs above and below the type) and is not transcribed.

uncertain.text: Seigneur Dieu ne ſ'eſt pas contenté de nons inſtruire
uncertain.note: sic: 'nons' for 'nous'. Checked at 4x: both letters are n, with no u anywhere in the word.

uncertain.text: deur de quelque calomnie, il ſ'emflãboit de cou roux ſi
uncertain.note: the print sets 'cou roux' with a full word-space inside what the sense wants as the single word 'couroux' (courroux); the gap measures the same as the neighbouring word spaces on this justified line. Transcribed as printed, two tokens. Under the word-division rule (§1) it could equally be closed up to 'couroux', as reader B did for 'Mart in' on p030; the reconciler should decide which way this class of justification gap goes.

uncertain.text: lomniateurs, preſte la main a leur malice, & les ſouſtiẽt
uncertain.note: same case as line 38: the print sets 'preſt e la main' with a gap before the final e of 'preſte'; normalized to 'preſte'. The tilde of 'ſouſtiẽt' is a wavy bar at 8x, not an acute, so 'ẽ' not 'é'.
the mark after 'vij' has a tail descending below the baseline at 8x, so it is transcribed as a comma; every other citation in this margin ends with a point, so it may be a point with a broken foot.
